body:
## Summary

During NF re-entry on Debian Trixie, the installed `/opt/noemaforge` payload was found to be owned by the invoking desktop user (`cat:cat`) and broadly group-writable. This is a packaging/install-process issue, not a host/GPU/runtime issue.

The local repair was:

```bash
sudo chown -R root:root /opt/noemaforge
sudo find /opt/noemaforge -type d -exec chmod 0755 {} \;
sudo find /opt/noemaforge -type f -exec chmod 0644 {} \;
sudo chmod 0755 \
  /opt/noemaforge/bin/* \
  /opt/noemaforge/tools/ops/*.sh \
  /opt/noemaforge/tools/prep/*.sh \
  2>/dev/null || true
```

After this repair, `noemaforge trixie-preflight --json` still passed, confirming the repair did not break the installed runtime surface.

## Evidence

The installed payload scan showed files and directories like:

```text
drwxrwxr-x cat:cat /opt/noemaforge
-rw-rw-r-- cat:cat /opt/noemaforge/lib/noemaforge-common.sh
-rw-rw-r-- cat:cat /opt/noemaforge/configs/tool-registry.yaml
-rw-rw-r-- cat:cat /opt/noemaforge/configs/tool-policy.yaml
-rw-rw-r-- cat:cat /opt/noemaforge/configs/*.json|*.yaml
```

`toolproxy diag` also reported installed config ownership as `cat:cat`:

```text
tool_registry: -rw-rw-r-- 664 cat:cat regular file /opt/noemaforge/configs/tool-registry.yaml
tool_policy: -rw-rw-r-- 664 cat:cat regular file /opt/noemaforge/configs/tool-policy.yaml
```

## Why this matters

`/opt/noemaforge` is an installed runtime payload used by systemd services. It should not remain writable by the interactive user/group after install. Otherwise, installed scripts/configs can be modified outside the expected release/update path, which weakens runtime integrity and makes diagnostics harder.

## Expected behavior

The installer should install `/opt/noemaforge` with explicit ownership and modes:

```text
/opt/noemaforge directories: root:root 0755
regular files:              root:root 0644
runtime executables/scripts: root:root 0755
mutable state:              outside /opt, e.g. /var/lib/noemaforge owned by noemaforge:noemaforge as needed
```

## Suggested fix

1. Add a post-copy ownership/mode normalization step to the installer.
2. Keep mutable state under `/var/lib/noemaforge`, `/run/noemaforge`, or another documented state path, not writable `/opt`.
3. Add a post-install verification command that fails if any `/opt/noemaforge` file is owned by the invoking user or group-writable unexpectedly.
4. Add CI/release-artifact checks for the installed layout, not just the source tree.

## Related

Related but separate from #212, which covers executable bits for smoke/preflight scripts. This issue covers ownership and writable installed payload integrity.
title: Installer installs /opt/noemaforge as invoking user and group-writable instead of root-owned runtime payload
